newsitem.title: UK: Minister rules Britain joining EMU in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Minister rules Britain joining EMU in 1999.

text.p: Health Secretary Stephen Dorrell on Sunday ruled out Britain joining a single European currency on its launch date of January 1, 1999.

The Conservative government, wary of party mutinies over Britain's role in Europe, has in the past adopted a "wait-and-see" attitude to the currency and ministers said they did not expect the project to be launched on time.

Prime Minister John Major, battling to keep his party united in the runup to the election due by May, has said it is "very unlikely, though not impossible" that Britain may join in the first wave in 1999.
But Dorrell, seen as a contender for the party leadership should Major step down after the forthcoming election, adopted a much blunter stance when interviewed by GMTV on Sunday.
"The Government's position, I would have thought, on the single currency is now as clear as you could ask for it to be," he said.

"And that is: first of all, no single currency without a referendum and, secondly, we shan't be joining a single currency on January 1, 1999, but we think that Britain ought to continue to participate in the discussion and take a decision subject to a referendum on Britain's interests alone."
